transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Well, I'm here because I just keep forgetting things lately. What finally made me ask for help is that I'm dropping the ball on little daily tasks I normally handle fine. Like, I'll forget to return important phone calls, or I'll completely forget to turn in a registration form for something. Even just stopping to run a quick errand on my way home from work... it just slips my mind completely. It's starting to get frustrating.
Have you noticed any other changes besides your memory, like confusion, difficulty finding words, problems with coordination, or changes in your mood or behavior?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't have any confusion or trouble finding my words, and my coordination is fine. My mood is pretty much normal, too—aside from just being a bit frustrated with myself for dropping the ball lately. But no, none of those other things you mentioned.

Do you notice that you're forgetting things that happened recently, like what you had for breakfast or a conversation from earlier today, or are you also forgetting older memories that you should normally remember?

No, it's not like that. I can remember what I had for breakfast, and I remember conversations just fine. And my older memories are all still there. It's really just... the tasks. The things I'm supposed to *do*. It's not like I'm losing my memory of what happened, I'm just forgetting to do the things I need to get done.
Do you find yourself forgetting to do things even when they’re written down or you’ve set reminders for them?

Well, no, not usually. If I actually write it down or set an alarm on my phone, I'm usually okay. The problem is more that I just don't think to write it down in the moment, or I tell myself I'll remember it without needing a reminder, and then... I don't. But if it's on a sticky note right in front of me, I'll get it done.
Do you find it hard to start tasks or follow through on them, even if you remember they need to be done?

Yeah, I do. Especially if it's something that takes a lot of focus. Like, if an assignment means sitting down to read a long chapter of something, or having to write out a whole plan... I just keep putting it off. I know I need to do it, but I'll delay it until it's really late, and then I end up rushing through it after work just to get it done.
Do you have trouble organizing tasks or figuring out the steps you need to take to get something done?

Yeah, lately I do. I mean, I can usually keep up with my job just fine, but since I started taking these evening classes, everything's just gotten... messy. My desk at home, my class folder, all the email reminders I get—they just turn into these big piles. I end up wasting a lot of time just trying to figure out what I'm even supposed to be doing first instead of actually doing it.
Have you had trouble with forgetfulness or staying organized like this before, or is this something that's only started recently?

No, it's definitely not just a recent thing. I mean, even way back in elementary school, I was always that kid. The one who forgot permission slips or somehow lost my homework in the bottom of my backpack. I always needed my mom or my teachers to remind me, step by step, just to get through a project and actually finish it.
So you mentioned having trouble with forgetfulness and organization since elementary school — have these problems continued throughout your life, like during high school, college, or work years?

Well, they've always kind of been there in the background, but... I'd say it hasn't always been this much of an issue. It really just became noticeably harder to manage since I started that evening certificate program. That was about 15 months ago. Before that, I was doing mostly fine just keeping up with my job, but adding the classes just made the attention and organization stuff a lot harder to deal with.

Do you find that these problems with forgetfulness and staying organized affect you mostly in one place, like just at home or just at work and school, or do they happen in multiple areas of your life?

I guess it's a little bit of everywhere. Like I mentioned, my desk at home is pretty messy right now with all the school stuff. But it definitely affects me at work, too. I'm a secretary, so being organized is basically my whole job... and lately I'm just having a harder time keeping track of everything there as well. So, yeah, it's not just in one place, it's happening in multiple areas of my life.
When you were a child, did your difficulties with forgetfulness and organization cause problems in different settings, like at home, at school, or with friends?

I'm not entirely sure, honestly. I know it was definitely an issue at school, like I mentioned before with the permission slips and homework. But as far as at home or with friends... I don't really remember it causing big problems there when I was a kid. Or at least, nothing that stands out to me now.
